persona.who: 19, second-year engineering student in Delhi, lives in a hostel, parents in Kanpur paid a lot for coaching. Scrolls Instagram 6h a day. Speaks Hinglish.
persona.note: sem exams in 3 weeks and i cant focus for even 20 min, keep opening insta, and then at night i think papa paid 2 lakh for coaching and im wasting it

understanding.bridge: What you call a mind that won't settle is what the Upanishads call the mind running after results it cannot hold.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the panic, the phone, and the night-time guilt, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the fear of losing your father's faith is what multiplies the worry, not the exam itself.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what is real in you cannot be taken by a result you have not yet written.
week_beats.act: You try focusing on one thing for twenty minutes, then let go of the result, and let the phone wait.
week_beats.story: A student who could not focus before his final exams shows you what steadying the mind looks like from the inside.

understanding.core_struggle: Panicked by exams in three weeks, unable to focus, and guilty about wasting his father's money and hope.
understanding.mirror: You open the phone to escape the replaying, and then the replaying starts again at night.
understanding.insight: Most of what you fear hasn't happened. Your mind keeps living it in advance, again and again.

queries.hook: The mind won't settle, the phone opens itself, and at night the father's money and the father's face come back.
queries.diagnose: Fear grows from imagining the future and from forgetting that what is real in us cannot be lost; worry multiplies what has not happened.
queries.steady: What is real in you cannot be taken by a result you have not yet written; the effort is yours and the result is not.
queries.act: Practise focusing on one thing for twenty minutes, then let go of the result; let the phone wait and let the night pass.
queries.story: A student who could not focus before his final exams, who was afraid of letting his father down, and who found a way to steady his mind.

weeks: What is real cannot be lost

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.meaning: Bhasa and Vilasa are two old friends who meet again after many years. One of them admits he never found peace. He explains that his mind is always caught in endless lists of what he has done, what he is doing, and what he must do. It is carried along on great waves of tasks. The depths of his mind dance with worry. He says this bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints. Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
verse.for_you: The panic you feel before your exams and the guilt about your father's money are like this bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings. Today, when you open Instagram, you are not just wasting time. You are letting the mind faint.

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Sugriva panics on seeing two armed strangers; Hanuman tells him his fear is getting ahead of the facts.
verse.sanskrit: अहो शाखामृगत्वं ते व्यक्तमेव प्लवङ्गम। लघुचित्ततयात्मानं न स्थापयसि यो मतौ।। ।॥
verse.line: Your mind keeps jumping, so you can't settle on a clear thought.
verse.translation: Clearly your restless monkey nature is showing, friend: because your mind is so flighty, you cannot settle yourself on a clear thought.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Hanuman sees Sugriva, the exiled monkey king, trembling on the mountain. Two armed strangers appear, and Sugriva panics, convinced his brother has sent killers to finish him. Hanuman speaks with a calm, clear voice. He tells him that his mind is running ahead of what is actually in front of him. The fear is real, but the danger is not yet there. He says that a restless mind keeps jumping from one thing to the next, and that is why Sugriva cannot hold on to a single clear thought.
verse.for_you: You are panicking about the exam, but your mind is running the scene before it even happens. Like Sugriva, you are seeing the danger that is not there yet. Let that thought sit with you. The exam is three weeks away, and the fear is jumping faster than the facts.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that his right is only to the action itself, never to the fruits of that action. He urges him not to let the fear of a bad outcome stop him from doing the work. The teaching is to give your full attention to the step in front of you, and then let go of the result. Care deeply, plan well, and aim true, but do not let the outcome own your mind or your peace.
verse.for_you: The result of the exam is not yours to hold yet. Your part is to sit with your books and give them your attention for twenty minutes, and then let go. What is real in you, your effort, cannot be taken by a mark you have not yet written.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on the mark of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: अनागतानां भोगानामवाञ्छनमकृत्रिमम् । आगतानां च संभोग इति पण्डितलक्षणम् ॥
verse.line: Not pining for pleasures still to come, and enjoying the ones already here: that is wisdom.
verse.translation: Not longing for pleasures yet to come, and enjoying those that have come: this, unforced, is the mark of the wise.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a free person does not waste energy chasing what is not yet here, nor do they ignore what is already here. This is the mark of someone who is truly wise. It means you can do the work in front of you without letting your mind run ahead to a future result it cannot yet hold.
verse.for_you: The twenty minutes you gave your books today were real, even if your mind was on the exam result. Let that small, present effort be enough for now. You do not have to hold the future yet.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥
verse.line: Yoga is unhooking from sorrow. Practise it with resolve and a heart that doesn't lose hope.
verse.translation: Know that to be yoga: the breaking of contact with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and with an undespairing mind.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that yoga is the breaking of contact with sorrow. It should be practiced with determination and without despair, by returning the mind gently again and again, like a lamp in a windless place.
verse.for_you: Right now, set a timer for twenty minutes and study one page. When the phone calls or the guilt pulls you back, bring your attention back to the words. You do not need to win the whole exam in one sitting.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verse.sanskrit: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
verse.line: Don't churn your mind with plans and second thoughts. Be still and rest in yourself.
verse.translation: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
verse.why: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to avoid decisions; decide, then stop churning.

prasang.title: You are not your mind
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra drives home that Janaka is not the body, the doer, or the mind's likes and dislikes, but the ocean in which the waves of life rise and fall. He urges faith, an end to grief, and rest from endless deliberation.
prasang.lesson: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, who is caught in the middle of his life. Janaka is a king, a husband, a man with duties, and he is standing at the edge of a crisis. Ashtavakra tells him not to stir his mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. He says be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self. This means you are the ocean, not the waves. Let them rise and fall without losing yourself.
verse.for_you: Right now, your mind is churning with plans about the exams and doubts about your father's hope. Try setting a timer for twenty minutes. Open only your textbook and do that one thing. When the timer goes off, close the book and let the result wait.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

story.hook_title: King Janaka overheard a song in his garden that he couldn't stop thinking about
story.teaser: King Janaka overheard a song in his garden that he couldn't stop thinking about
story.for_you: King Janaka was a king with duties, just like you have exams. He heard something that shook him, but he did not run away. He got up and did his work with a mind that did not clutch. You can do the same. You do not have to fix everything today.

script: You are carrying a panic that does not belong to this room, and a guilt that feels heavier than the books on your desk. You are here with exams in three weeks, and your mind cannot sit still for twenty minutes. It is exhausting to feel this trapped in your own head.

Bhasa and Vilasa are two old friends who meet again after many years. They grew up together in a forest hermitage, and after their fathers died they drifted apart, spending lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well. Bhasa said:
उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु, क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम्. इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम्, कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी.
In plain words: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.

He is saying that the mind is carried along on great waves of tasks, and its depths dance with worry. The bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints. What is hard is that this happens even after years of effort. You can study hard, you can try to focus, but if the mind is running after results it cannot hold, it will exhaust itself. The truth underneath is that the panic you feel has not happened yet. It lives only in the lists your mind keeps making.

When you open Instagram, your mind is not just resting. It is letting the bird of your mind faint in a net of reckonings. You are giving your attention to a world that will not hold you, because the world of exams and results feels too tight. Try to close the app and give your attention to one thing for just one minute.
What if the list in your head could wait until tomorrow?

depth.life: You are sitting with your books and your phone is open. Every time you look up, the screen is in your hands again. The guilt about your father's money sits heavy, and the exams feel like a storm you cannot outrun. Your mind is running on a track it built itself, and you are just riding it.
depth.points: The mind is not a tool you are using. It is a bird caught in a net of its own making. It faints because it is trying to hold every moment at once, past and future, all at the same time.
depth.practice: Put your phone face down and set a timer for five minutes. Let your mind wander wherever it wants, but keep your eyes on the page.
depth.question: What does the mind want to do if you let it rest for just five minutes?
